thread.title: California has the highest poverty rate in the US; Arizona not far behind

author: Mike Sunnucks
title: California has the highest poverty rate in the US; Arizona not far behind
text: – Senior Reporter, Phoenix Business Journal Jan 17, 2018, 9:58am MST California — with its wealth, Silicon Valley, Hollywood and liberal politics — has the highest poverty rate in the U.S. when cost-of-living is combined with income levels. Arizona — which likes to contrast its costs, business and political climates to California — isn’t far behind and has the fifth highest poverty rate when living costs are include in poverty statistics. That is according Supplemental Poverty Measures reported by the U.S. Census Bureau. Arizona has a 17.5 percent poverty rate, according the SPM measure which adds in cost of living, housing and utility bills to income levels. That is fifth highest in the U.S. behind only California (20.6 percent), Florida (19.0 percent), Louisiana and New York (both at 17.9 percent), according to the Census Bureau. California — which is home to mega companies such as Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL), Walt Disney Co. (NYSE: DIS), Intel (Nasdaq: INTC), Facebook (NYSE: FB) and Google parent Alphabet (Nasdaq: GOOGL) — has tons of wealth and does well on economic indicators such as per capita GDP and workforce participation rate. But California’s high cost of living — especially in San Francisco, San Diego, Silicon Valley and Los Angeles where real estate costs are astronomical compared to Phoenix — coupled with its high number of immigrant and other workers in lower paying jobs makes household budgets tight and drives up its SPM poverty rate. The official poverty rate — which just looks at income — ranks California tied for 17th in the U.S. with a 15 percent rate. New Mexico has the highest rate on the traditional measure at 22 percent, according to Census data. As for Arizona, the state has an 18.8 percent poverty rate under the traditional income measure. That is also fifth highest among U.S. states behind only New Mexico, Louisiana (21.7 percent), Kentucky (20.7 percent) and Mississippi (20.2 percent). Arizona has long attracted businesses, jobs, real estate investors and transplants from California. Some of them are seeking lower costs, more business friendly climates and more conservative politics and culture. A number of major California companies including Intel and Apple also have operations in Phoenix. – Senior Reporter, Phoenix Business Journal Jan 17, 2018, 9:58am MST
